claims.text: CodePipeline's default execution mode is `SUPERSEDED`.
In CodePipeline's `SUPERSEDED` execution mode, a stage is locked to one execution at a time.

In CodePipeline's `SUPERSEDED` mode, a newer execution can overtake and supersede an earlier execution that is still waiting to enter a locked stage, dropping it before it starts; an execution that is already running in the stage is protected.

If a CodeBuild stage running `pulumi up` is busy and enough commits land, a queued execution waiting behind it in a `SUPERSEDED` CodePipeline pipeline can be superseded and never run, silently skipping a deployment.
Setting the CodePipeline pipeline's execution mode to `QUEUED` makes waiting executions form a queue and each one runs in turn rather than being superseded by later executions.
CodePipeline's `QUEUED` execution mode requires a V2 pipeline (`pipelineType` V2).
The AWS CLI's `create-pipeline` and `update-pipeline` commands can set `executionMode` and `pipelineType` for a CodePipeline pipeline.
The `aws.codepipeline.Pipeline` resource in the Pulumi AWS provider accepts `executionMode` and `pipelineType` inputs.

The `aws.codepipeline.Pipeline` resource is described below in the same page (in the 'Manage the pipeline with Pulumi' section), and its registry API docs page exists at /registry/packages/aws/api-docs/codepipeline/pipeline/.
The AWS CodePipeline user guide page 'concepts-how-it-works' documents CodePipeline execution modes.
When two runs reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one of them.
When two runs reach the same Pulumi stack at once, the run that does not get the lease has its `pulumi up` fail with an update conflict error.
Azure Pipelines supports an exclusive lock check on an environment, which can prevent concurrent deployments to the environment targeted by a deployment job.
The link to the Update conflicts troubleshooting page (/docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/) targets an existing page.
In Azure DevOps, the exclusive lock check is added from the environment's 'Approvals and checks' tab.
Azure Pipelines stages support a `lockBehavior` property that controls how the stage interacts with exclusive lock checks.
`lockBehavior` accepts the values `sequential` and `runLatest`, and the default is `runLatest`.
The `Pulumi@1` Azure Pipelines task accepts `command`, `stack`, and `args` inputs, with `command: up` and `args: --yes` used to deploy.
With `lockBehavior: runLatest`, only the most recently queued run acquires the exclusive lock, and older runs waiting behind it are passed over (cancelled/skipped) rather than eventually applied.
With `lockBehavior: sequential`, every queued stage run acquires the exclusive lock in order, one at a time.
Pulumi Cloud serializes updates to a stack, running them one at a time.
The Azure DevOps provider in the Pulumi Registry has a `azuredevops.CheckExclusiveLock` resource that manages the exclusive lock check as code.
The link /registry/packages/azuredevops/api-docs/checkexclusivelock/ targets an existing Registry API docs page for the CheckExclusiveLock resource.
When two runs of the same TeamCity build configuration reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one of them.
When two concurrent builds target the same Pulumi stack, the build that does not get the lease has its `pulumi up` fail with an update conflict error.
TeamCity's default is to let build configurations run concurrently against as many free agents as are available.
The docs page at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ exists and describes update conflicts.
TeamCity's build configuration advanced option 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' is located under the configuration's General Settings.
The default value of TeamCity's 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' option is 0, meaning unlimited.
Setting TeamCity's 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' to 1 causes a second build to be queued and run only after the first finishes.
Pulumi Cloud's per-stack lease gives one-at-a-time update behavior for a stack.
In Azure Pipelines, adding an exclusive lock check to the environment targeted by the deployment job serializes Pulumi deployments (prevents concurrent runs).
In Azure Pipelines YAML, `lockBehavior: sequential` is a valid setting on a stage, used together with an environment exclusive lock check.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/azure-devops/ has a section anchored 'serialize-deployments-with-an-exclusive-lock'.
In AWS CodePipeline, setting the pipeline's execution mode to `QUEUED` makes waiting executions run in turn.
AWS CodePipeline's default execution mode (SUPERSEDED) lets a newer execution supersede an older execution that is still waiting to start.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/aws-code-services/ has a section anchored 'serialize-pipeline-executions'.
In TeamCity, setting the build configuration option 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' to 1 prevents concurrent runs of the deployment build.
TeamCity build configurations have a setting named 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds'.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/teamcity/ has a section anchored 'limit-concurrent-builds' (the TeamCity guide).
